mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 5.25% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by at least 0.25 percentage points over 8 weeks
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 8-week pre-trend period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month rolling window, the 20-day forward return correlation with the labor strength signal is <0.2 (Spearman's rho).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly retail sales (not in observable list, so skip) — instead, use HOUST as a proxy for demand — surge by 3% or more from the prior month, the S&P 500 anticipates future consumer demand growth and posts positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: In 30% of months with a >3% HOUST increase, the 5-day forward return is non-positive (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply chains, prompting market participants to price in a slower economic recovery and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During 10 such INDPRO contractions, the 20-day forward return median is not significantly negative (median > 0 with IQR upper > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 expects the Fed to maintain higher policy rates, which typically depresses equity valuations and yields negative 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 such CPIAUCSL high-inflation months, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically lower than during low-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unionized employment (PAYEMS) without a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE) suggest labor market resilience, which typically precedes equity market strength and positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for three consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 6.5%
failure_condition: In 40% of such labor growth episodes, the 20-day forward return is non-positive (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained downward trend in all major macro proxies (GDPC1, RSAFS, HOUST) over the prior 12 months indicates an economic contraction, which historically precedes S&P 500 bearish sentiment and negative 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 24 contraction episodes, the 60-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (median > 0 with IQR upper > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, it signals a potential policy easing cycle that typically supports equity valuations, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 20 such easing anticipation periods, the 5-day forward return is non-positive in >50% cases (binomial test p < 0.05).
